skills.name: Resume-JD Optimizer
skills.description: Generates a tailored two-page resume and matching cover letter from a job description and a master resume, in a plain human-written style, enforced by blocking build gates.
skills.author: Resume Generator Team

inputs.name: jd_path
inputs.description: Path to the job description. Namespaced by worktree so concurrent sessions do not share one posting (default: input/jd-{worktree}.txt, falling back to input/jd.txt)

inputs.name: resume_path
inputs.description: Path to master resume file (default: input/master-resume.md)

inputs.name: track_resume_paths
inputs.description: Per-track master resumes, selected from the JD's role responsibilities. Skills come from these; facts always come from input/master-resume.md (default: input/master-resume-{track}.md)

inputs.name: output_dir
inputs.description: Output directory for the generated files (default: output/{YYYYMMDD})

outputs.name: tailored_resume
outputs.description: Markdown resume conforming to the output contract in scripts/convert_resume.py

outputs.name: cover_letter
outputs.description: Matching cover letter, generated from the finished resume

outputs.name: optimization_summary
outputs.description: Chat-only report: tracks selected, keyword coverage, requirements deliberately not claimed, entries omitted for missing detail, and the data/ files written

outputs.name: new_skills_log
outputs.description: JD skills with no match in any master resume, grouped by track and appended for later review. Written instead of asking the user

outputs.name: master_resume_gaps_log
outputs.description: Anything that made the run weaker than it should have been: unmet must-haves, missing metrics, thin track files, drift between a track file and the master. Grouped by track and appended

features: Skill Gap Analysis with Human Confirmation

success_metrics.length: Two pages, roughly 900 words, never above 1050
success_metrics.gates: All five gates in scripts/verify_resume.py pass without --no-verify
success_metrics.ats_keywords: Every must-have JD keyword present, none more than three times
success_metrics.requirement_coverage: All MUST-HAVE JD requirements addressed or explicitly reported as unmet
success_metrics.factual_accuracy: Every company, date, location and credential verified against the master resume
success_metrics.emphasis: Zero inline bold outside technical-skill labels
success_metrics.production_ready: Ready for actual job submission with no manual cleanup

constraints: Never fabricate experience, dates, job titles, certifications or metrics
Never generate a certification, and never emit an AI-generated marker
Never leave a bracketed placeholder in the deliverable; omit the entry and report the gap in chat
Never claim a JD-only skill; detecting one and logging it is not evidence the candidate has it
Never stop to ask the user mid-run; log the uncertainty to data/ and finish the deliverable
Never source a smart-contract, protocol or audit role from master-resume-blockchain.md
Facts always come from input/master-resume.md, never from a track file
No em dashes, arrows, emoji or AI-register phrasing
No inline bold outside technical-skill labels
Report unmet requirements every run rather than narrowing the keyword list until it scores 100%
Never read another worktree's jd-*.txt, even when the expected one is missing

research_basis.ats_evolution: Modern ATS use ML for contextual relevance scoring
research_basis.quantified_metrics: Numbers parse as structured data and score higher
research_basis.keyword_strategy: Natural integration (1-3x) works better than stuffing
research_basis.keyword_emphasis: Bolding is invisible to ATS and costs human readability when overused, so it is not used
research_basis.formatting: Single serif typeface, greyscale, plain text, no tables or graphics, optimal for parsing
research_basis.length: Two pages is the practical ceiling for recruiter review at this experience level

example_workflow.step1: Put the posting in input/jd-{worktree}.txt, where {worktree} is the repo directory name. The master resumes are already in place
example_workflow.step2: Run the skill. It does not stop to ask anything
example_workflow.step3: Skill picks the matching master-resume-{track}.md files from the JD's role responsibilities
example_workflow.step4: Skill writes the resume and cover letter to output/{YYYYMMDD}/
example_workflow.step5: Skill appends anything new or missing to data/new-skills-{worktree}.md and data/master-resume-gaps-{worktree}.md
example_workflow.step6: Review the chat report, especially 'Not claimed' and 'Omitted for missing detail'
example_workflow.step8: At the weekend, work through the two data/ files and fold real skills into the master resumes

repository.name: resume-generator
repository.description: Comprehensive resume optimization and generation toolkit
